story: Māui was born prematurely and, fearing he would become a malevolent spirit, his mother Taranga cast him into the sea wrapped in her hair. Ocean spirits wrapped him in seaweed, and his grandfather found him on the beach and raised him. Māui later joined his family, where his four brothers and sister Hina at first distrusted him but came to admire his shapeshifting powers. Noticing his mother vanished each dawn, Māui blocked the light and followed her, transformed into a bird, down into the underworld. There he found his parents, and his father performed his birth ritual incorrectly, causing the gods to curse Māui and all humanity with mortality. Using a magic fishhook made from his grandmother's jawbone, Māui secretly joined his brothers on a fishing trip, baited the hook with his own blood, and hauled up a giant fish that became a great island. His brothers cut into the fish before proper rites were performed, causing it to writhe and form mountains and valleys instead of flat land. Māui also stole fire by exhausting the fingernails of the fire goddess, escaping her wrathful flames with help from weather gods, and brought back fire-making sticks for his people. He transformed his sister's husband into the first dog after a quarrel, causing his sister to drown herself in grief. Finally, seeking immortality for humankind, Māui attempted to pass through the body of the goddess of death while she slept, but a companion laughed and woke her; she crushed him, making him the first to die and dooming all humans to mortality.
